A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReasonBrain framework and Reason50K dataset. All 22 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent matching the material.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, human evaluations, and supplementary experiments in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, backbone experiments, interaction ablations, and instruction-conversion evaluations in Section 4 and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The proposed FRCE branches, ID Controller, MLLM/QFormer guidance, CME, and training objectives remain unchanged. Backbone substitutions are evaluated as variants; the contradictory backbone descriptions introduced in Table A6 do not establish a change to the default method.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on Complex-Edit, covering explicit instructions with varying complexity and multiple editing operations, in Figure 5. Reason50K, ReasonEdit, EditWorld, MagicBrush, and Emu Edit remain. The training dataset and four reasoning categories are unchanged; multi-step hypothetical editing was already evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 substantially expand quantitative comparisons with MIGE, SmartFreeEdit, Bagel/Bagel-Thinking, Flux Kontext, Qwen-Image-Edit, ChatGPT-4o, and GPT Image 1.5; Table 2 also includes fine-tuned Qwen-Image-Edit. Figure 5 removes PixWizard and adds MGIE, Qwen-Image-Edit, and GPT Image 1.5 while retaining InstructPix2Pix and SmartEdit. Table A11 introduces instruction-conversion pipelines as comparators.

E3.justification: v3 adds backbone comparisons with and without FRCE/CME, interaction-removal controls, and three instruction converters paired with fine-tuned InstructPix2Pix or zero-shot Flux/Qwen editors. These introduce substantial new evaluation designs. The 400-per-category validation split and main training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Table A6 newly specifies SD backbones despite Appendix E retaining FLUX.1-dev, leaving that setting unresolved.

E4.justification: New analyses test backbone dependence, FRCE–diffusion binding, CME directionality, and whether explicit instruction conversion can substitute for ReasonBrain (Table 5 and Tables A3–A4/A11). New snowman and dropped-egg cases extend qualitative ablations. Table A1 regroups existing Table 4 results; the multi-step, data-generation, and one-to-many studies were already present in v2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The existing ten-annotator alignment assessment and 30-participant, 50-image preference study retain their sample sizes and aggregation practices.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive baseline, Complex-Edit, backbone, interaction, and conversion-pipeline results. Default ReasonBrain totals in Table 2 remain 0.259/0.877/0.847 for CLIP/MLLM/Ins-Align. Figure 5 revises retained results, including ReasonBrain’s ReasonEdit Ins-Align from 93.1% to 79.5%, and removes external-benchmark CLIP entries. Table A6 reverses v2 Table A2’s 3B/7B score and timing assignments, contradicting its accompanying prose.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Equations 1–3 and the training objectives in Appendix D, Equations A1–A2, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: HI-IE, the 51,039-sample Reason50K dataset, the FRCE/CME-based ReasonBrain framework, and strong reasoning and zero-shot generalization. Additional experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantial interpretations of backbone dependence, reasoning–editing interaction, and shortcomings of instruction conversion. Section 4.2 defends some scene changes as necessary for expressing hypothetical events, while Appendix I newly acknowledges excessive global appearance changes and proposes stronger style constraints. Section 4.1 also qualifies performance dominance from all metrics to almost all metrics.

D1.justification: Table A6 adds component/trainable parameter counts and backbone descriptions for the 7B/3B variants. The abstract changes a promised public release to 'Code is released,' although Appendix A retains future-release wording. Most implementation and hardware details remain unchanged. The new SD backbone labels conflict with Appendix E’s FLUX.1-dev description, reducing the clarity of the added documentation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Bagel, Flux Kontext, and Qwen-Image and expands positioning against Complex-Edit’s explicit, multi-operation instructions. Complex-Edit, MIGE, and SmartFreeEdit were already cited in v2; publication and title updates for retained works do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized introduction and discussion rewrites, updates author order and affiliations, and reorganizes the appendices into framework-design discussion, other quantitative results, and limitations. It also adds acknowledgments and a conflict disclosure and relocates the impact statement. The main section sequence and most method, dataset-generation, and training prose remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to two columns. Table 1 is transposed, Tables 2–3 expand, and identity-preservation results move into Table 2. Figure 5 is redrawn without its CLIP panel; Figure 6 gains comparator columns; Figure 7 replaces the paint example with a snowman. Four appendix qualitative grids are consolidated into Figure A3, retaining their examples at smaller size.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline and backbone comparisons, direct instruction-conversion controls, and explicit style/identity limitations improve scrutiny of the existing claims. These gains are tempered by new reporting inconsistencies: Table A6 reverses the 3B/7B results and conflicts with the retained backbone description, while Appendix F describes Table A3’s MLLM-score decrease as a human-evaluation finding. The added evidence therefore provides a limited net quality improvement.
